paragraphs: Red Lions came through 3-2 after a match that swung back and forth in extra time. Fox put Red Lions ahead in the 28th minute from Lane’s assist, Gray levelled for Blue Sharks in the 62nd with Frost involved, Reid restored the lead in the 95th from Rook’s pass, and Cruz brought Blue Sharks back at 105 minutes with Wells supplying the pass. The final twist came in the 113th minute, when Bell put the ball into the Red Lions net for the decisive own goal.

Red Lions were the stronger side for most of the night. They had 27 shots to 15, 11 on target to 7, and 6 big chances to 5, while their passing was far cleaner with 776 completed passes from 838 attempts, compared with Blue Sharks’ 321 from 376. Red Lions also spent far more of the match in advanced areas, with a much higher average line and 110 entries into the final third to 31.

The last stretch was messy rather than controlled, even though Red Lions still had most of the ball and territory. In the final ten minutes, Red Lions had 79 possession and 91 field tilt, but Blue Sharks kept finding ways to stay alive and force the game into chaos. Reid’s 95th-minute strike looked like it might set the tone, but Cruz answered quickly, and the own goal by Bell ended a match that stayed tense until the final whistle.
